analyst_view.overall: Two struggling sides meet at the WWK Arena: Augsburg (15th, 9 points) are seven league games without a win under Manuel Baum and have conceded at least twice in six of them, while Mainz (12th, 10 points) have lost four competitive games in a row, though Urs Fischer was pleased with the display against Bayern. Augsburg are without Banks, Matsima, Massengo and Brackelmann (now with an infection after his concussion), and one more defender is uncertain, so the back three from the start of the season is gone; the numbers count the four named absences, including about +6% on Mainz's goals for each missing regular defender. Mainz miss Kohr until January and Silas is not yet ready, also counted. Both coaches expect a tight game decided by duels; Fischer calls Augsburg quick on the break with Gregoritsch as target man and a set-piece threat, and Gregoritsch is expected to start again. Referee Martin Petersen's high card record (4.5 a game, +14%) is in the numbers, as is both sides' leaky recent form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already lifted by both leaky defences' recent form and counting Brackelmann, Massengo and Matsima out (Augsburg lose some goals, Mainz gain about 6% per missing defender). Baum admits the defence is patched up, but that is what the numbers already carry, and Gregoritsch returning to the starting side is his normal role, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Augsburg winning slightly more at home and Mainz's wing-backs Caci and Mwene expected to start. Both teams are predicted in a back three with wing-backs, which matches their records, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already including about 14% for referee Petersen and Mainz's high recent count. Mainz's combative Kohr is out until January and Augsburg's Massengo also misses out; the numbers count both only for goals, not their bookings, so I trim 3%, to about 5.0, kept small because both Baum and Fischer expect a game of duels.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already lifted by Augsburg's big recent volume (+19%) and Mainz's (+7%). Fischer expects a compact Augsburg playing on the break and a tight game, which fits their record, so I stay at 31.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with momentum adding for both (+13% Augsburg, +6% Mainz). Augsburg's reshuffled back line is already in the numbers through the missing defenders, and the extra defender Baum called uncertain is unnamed, too vague to size, so I stay at 10.8.
